verses.text: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It’s good to thank the LORD and sing praise to your name, Most High,
to tell of your faithful love in the morning and your faithfulness every night,
with the ten-stringed lute, the harp, and the melody of the lyre.
What you’ve done fills me with joy, LORD. I’ll celebrate what your hands have made.
LORD, your works are amazing! Your thoughts go so deep.
People with no sense miss it. Fools can’t get their heads around this:
the wicked may pop up like grass and those who do evil may thrive, but they’ll be destroyed forever.
You, LORD, are on high forever.
Look, LORD, your enemies will perish. Every one of those evildoers will scatter.
But you’ve lifted my horn high like a wild ox’s. You’ve anointed me with fresh oil.
I’ve seen my enemies with my own eyes, and I’ve heard about the wicked who rise up against me.
The righteous will flourish like palm trees and grow tall like cedars in Lebanon.
Planted in the LORD’s house, they’ll flourish in the courts of our God.
Even in old age they’ll still bear fruit. They’ll stay green and full of sap,
showing that the LORD is upright. He’s my rock, and there’s no wrong in him.
